request:
Create a configurable streaming accumulator module named `stream_acc` with parameter `WIDTH` (default 16).

Ports: `clk` (input), `rst` (input, active-high synchronous reset), `in_valid` (input, 1 bit), `in_data` (input, WIDTH bits, unsigned), `in_last` (input, 1 bit), `in_ready` (output, 1 bit), `out_valid` (output, 1 bit), `out_data` (output, WIDTH bits), `out_ready` (input, 1 bit), `clear` (input, 1 bit).

Behavior: the module sums packets of unsigned words. A word is accepted at a rising clock edge when `in_valid` and `in_ready` are both 1. Each accepted word is added to an internal accumulator using saturating unsigned addition (the sum never exceeds 2^WIDTH-1). When the accepted word has `in_last`=1, the packet is complete: on the following cycle `out_valid` becomes 1 and `out_data` presents the saturated packet sum; they hold until the output handshake (`out_valid` and `out_ready` both 1 at a clock edge). After the handshake `out_valid` returns to 0 and the accumulator starts the next packet from 0. While an output is pending (`out_valid`=1) the module applies backpressure: `in_ready` is 0. Otherwise `in_ready` is 1. `in_ready` and `out_valid` depend only on the internal state (registered behaviour, no combinational path from `in_valid` or `out_ready`). `out_data` is 0 whenever `out_valid` is 0. `clear`, when 1 at a clock edge, has priority over everything else: it resets the accumulator to 0 and discards any pending output. Reset state: accumulator 0, `out_valid`=0, `in_ready`=1. Latency from the last accepted word to `out_valid` is exactly one cycle.
